requirement_text: Continuing for the 2027 application cycle, U-M will be test-optional. Prospective students will continue to have the choice to submit standardized test scores (ACT/SAT), if they desire, as part of their application. Advancement Placement (AP) scores, International Baccalaureate (IB) grades, and predicted results or other international credentials will be considered in context with the academic record, regardless of whether or not test-optional is chosen. The university will review the policy on an ongoing basis.
researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK (test-optional/required policy, the top risk flagged for this batch). This page's own title is 'New for 2026-2027 Application Cycle,' explicitly 'for entry in fall 2027,' so cycle_year=2027 is directly stated by the source, not inferred. Checked specifically for a live pandemic-era contradicting page: admissions.umich.edu/explore-visit/virtual-resources/covid-19-faqs (a URL surfaced by search) returned HTTP 403 Access Denied on direct fetch -- not a live page presenting contradicting current policy, so this is NOT recorded as CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE. Policy history for context only (not this record's source): a 'test-flexible' policy was adopted June 2020 for pandemic-era cycles, then formalized into a permanent test-optional policy in February 2024 per secondary press corroboration (Detroit News, Michigan Daily) -- consistent with, not contradicting, this current statement. A second official page (Ross School of Business undergraduate admissions) independently confirms the identical test-optional SUBSTANCE (same non-penalizing, self-report-allowed policy) but anchors its own 'effective since' language to 'the 2025 application cycle' rather than 2027 -- recorded as a separate, cross-referenced record (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0002) per the brief's instruction to record conflicts rather than silently pick the more current-looking page, even though this is a stale cycle-year LABEL rather than a substantive policy disagreement.

requirement_text: Effective for the 2025 application cycle, U-M and therefore Michigan Ross will be test optional. You have the choice to submit standardized test scores (ACT/SAT) as part of your application. Other test scores (AP, IB, PSAT) will no longer be considered in their place. The university will review the policy on an ongoing basis.
limitations: This page states the test-optional policy took effect 'for the 2025 application cycle' -- a different (older) cycle label than the central admissions Application Changes page's 'Continuing for the 2027 application cycle' framing (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0001). cycle_year deliberately left null rather than set to 2025, because it is unclear whether that figure uses the same entry-year convention as the rest of this batch (Fall 2027 = cycle_year 2027) or an older single-year labeling convention Ross has not refreshed. Do not silently normalize this record's cycle_year without human review.
researcher_notes: Checked for a genuine POLICY conflict (per this batch's top-priority trap) and found none in substance: both pages agree the SAT/ACT is optional, non-penalizing, and self-reportable; the only discrepancy is which cycle-year the 'effective since' framing cites. Most likely explanation is that this Ross-specific page has simply not been refreshed with a newer cycle label since the policy was first announced, while the central admissions page has been kept current -- but per the research brief's instruction ('record BOTH as separate requirement records ... do not pick the more current-looking one'), this is recorded as its own row rather than silently merged into or discarded in favor of REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0001. Cross-reference REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0001 for the current, cycle-2027-labeled statement.

requirement_text: If English is your second language, you must take the TOEFL, IELTS, ECPE, CAE or CPE, PTE Academic, or MET examination and earn a passing score in one of the following acceptable ranges: TOEFL (iBT, including the Home Edition): 100 range with section scores 23+ in listening & reading and 21+ in speaking and writing.
limitations: Exception on the same page: applicants are exempted from this entire test requirement if SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing >= 650 (or old-SAT critical reading >= 600) or both ACT Reading and English >= 27, combined with 4+ recent years of academic study in a named list of countries -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0010. Do not evaluate a missing English-test score as not_met without first checking that exemption.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK: this is the legacy/original 0-120 TOEFL iBT scale (with per-section sub-scores on the original 0-30 scale). The source page does not itself attach an explicit 'before Jan 21, 2026' date qualifier to THIS specific bullet -- that boundary is inferred from the immediately adjacent bullet's own explicit label, '(launching Jan. 21, 2026)' (see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0004), which implies this unlabeled line is the pre-cutover scale. This inference is flagged, not silently assumed, per the scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md finding. Checked for the Glasgow-style partial-unsatisfiability defect: the overall (100) and per-section floors (23/23/21/21, summing to a minimum of 88) are mutually satisfiable on the SAME legacy scale, so this requirement is NOT partially unsatisfiable, unlike the Glasgow case.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (launching Jan. 21, 2026): 5-6 range with section scores of 5+ (CEFR C1)
limitations: Same SAT/ACT-based exemption pathway applies as REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0003 -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0010.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK: this is ETS's new 1-6 TOEFL iBT scale, effective for tests taken on/after 2026-01-21 (per ETS's own transition, documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md, the new overall is the average of the four section scores). U-M's overall floor (5, within a 5-6 range) and per-section floor (5+) are on the SAME new 1-6 scale and are mutually consistent (four sections each >=5 necessarily average to >=5), so this requirement does NOT exhibit the Glasgow-style partial-unsatisfiability defect found elsewhere in this corpus -- it is fully satisfiable as published. Today's retrieval date (2026-08-21) is after the 2026-01-21 cutover, so this new-scale requirement is the one currently operative for newly-taken tests; the legacy-scale sibling record (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0003) remains relevant only for score reports from tests taken before the cutover (and, per ETS policy, via the comparable 0-120 score for up to two years post-cutover, which U-M's own page does not separately restate as its own threshold).

requirement_text: IELTS / IELTS Indicator: 7.0 range with section scores 6.5+
limitations: Same SAT/ACT-based exemption pathway applies -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0010.
researcher_notes: IELTS's 0-9 band scale is unaffected by the TOEFL rescale (confirmed unambiguous per the scale audit in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md). U-M's page treats standard IELTS and the online 'IELTS Indicator' as interchangeable for this threshold, combined into one source line, so recorded as one record rather than two.

requirement_text: ECPE: Certificate with all sections at least a C
limitations: Same SAT/ACT-based exemption pathway applies -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0010.
researcher_notes: Examination for the Certificate of Proficiency in English (ECPE, University of Michigan's own historical English-testing program, now operated by the University of Michigan's Center for the Assessment of Language). No test_scale enum value exists for a letter-grade-per-section certificate exam, left null rather than force-fit.

requirement_text: CAE (C1 Advanced): 185 with no less than 180+ in all sections (CEFR C1). CPE (C2 Proficiency): 185 with no less than 180+ in all sections (CEFR C1).
limitations: Same SAT/ACT-based exemption pathway applies -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0010. Minor whitespace-only normalization applied (source rendered 'CPE(C2' with no space); no wording changed.
researcher_notes: Cambridge English Qualifications C1 Advanced and C2 Proficiency are listed as two separate bullets on the source page but carry identical numeric thresholds (185 overall, 180+ per section), so combined into one record rather than two near-duplicate rows. Cambridge English Scale is unaffected by the TOEFL rescale; unambiguous per the scale audit in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md.

requirement_text: PTE Academic: 68 with all sections equally strong
limitations: Same SAT/ACT-based exemption pathway applies -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0010. 'All sections equally strong' is not a further-quantified figure on this page.
researcher_notes: No PTE-specific value exists in this batch's test_scale enum (TOEFL/IELTS/Cambridge/SAT only) -- left null rather than force-fit, consistent with the MIT batch's precedent for the same test. PTE Academic's own native scale is 10-90; U-M's figure of 68 is on that native scale.

requirement_text: MET: 64 with section scores of 59+ (4-skill MET-digital)
limitations: Same SAT/ACT-based exemption pathway applies -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0010.
researcher_notes: Michigan English Test (MET), 4-skill digital version. No test_scale enum value exists for MET -- left null rather than force-fit.

requirement_text: Exceptions: You can be exempted from taking any of these exams if your SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing score is 650 or above (600 or above if presenting an old SAT critical reading score), or if both your ACT Reading and English scores are 27 or above, and if you have recently completed at least four years of rigorous academic study in any of the following countries: Anguilla, Antigua, Barbuda, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Bermuda, British Virgin Islands, Canada (except Quebec), Cayman Islands, Dominica, England, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Montserrat, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Seychelles, Shetland Islands, St. Kitts-Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos Islands, United States (other than Puerto Rico), US Virgin Islands, Wales. (Those in American Schools and British Schools abroad may also be exempted if at least four years of rigorous academic study has recently been completed if scores meet above standards.) We do not offer intensive English make-up course work for conditional admission.
limitations: This is a named EXEMPTION (an inclusion, not an exclusion) requiring BOTH a qualifying SAT/ACT sub-score combination AND a specific country/school-of-study history -- a naive evaluator checking only 'was an English test submitted' could wrongly mark an exempt applicant as not_met. Both conditions (test sub-score AND country/duration) must hold; neither alone is sufficient per the source text ('...and if you have recently completed...').
researcher_notes: Flagged per this batch's named-exclusions/inclusions trap (scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md, section 3): a student's numeric SAT/ACT sub-scores alone do not resolve this fact without also knowing their country of recent academic study, which a bare threshold comparison cannot represent. Also folds in an adjacent negative fact from the same page for compactness rather than a near-empty extra row: U-M explicitly does not offer conditional admission with concurrent intensive English coursework as a fallback for applicants who do not meet the proficiency bar (its English Language Institute is described as being for already-enrolled students who already meet the proficiency requirements, not a conditional-admission pathway).

requirement_text: Ideally, you will have completed five units (full-year courses) during each of the four years and elected Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, honors, enriched, and accelerated high school courses when appropriate and available. You are required to complete four years of English, with at least two rigorous writing courses, at least two laboratory science courses, and electives from the subject groups listed below.
limitations: This is the university-wide floor. Individual first-year-admitting schools/colleges publish their own more specific unit counts by subject (English/World Language/Mathematics/Science/Social Studies/Other) on the same page -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0012 through REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0018.
researcher_notes: Page also states average admitted-student GPA is 3.9 -- a descriptive statistic, not an eligibility requirement, so not recorded as its own requirement row (consistent with this batch's discipline of not treating class profile statistics as requirements; see also research-handoff doc's precedent against inventing thresholds from descriptive stats).

Footnote: 'Students entering the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts are strongly encouraged to take four years of language study, with two years of the same world language required for admission (American Sign Language is included).'

Separately (out of scope for admission requirements): admissions.umich.edu's Application Changes page also states that beginning fall 2027, LSA will record all LSA first-year students' first-semester grades as pass/no-credit rather than a letter grade on external transcripts -- a post-matriculation academic policy, not an admission requirement or deadline, so not recorded as its own row in this admission-focused batch.

requirement_text: High School Course Expectations table cell (units of full-year courses): English 4, World Language 2, Mathematics 4, Science 4, Social Studies 3, Other electives 4. Footnote on the SAME page states a DIFFERENT, lower math figure: 'Students entering the School of Nursing are required to have completed three units of mathematics, and four units of science, with one unit each of biology and chemistry. Four units of mathematics are recommended.'
limitations: INTERNAL SOURCE DISCREPANCY on a single page: the table cell displays Mathematics=4 for Nursing, but the footnote's own prose says mathematics is 'required' at three units with four units merely 'recommended.' A downstream evaluator should treat the REQUIRED math floor for Nursing as 3 units (per the footnote's explicit 'required' language), with 4 as the recommended/table-displayed figure, but this is this researcher's interpretation of an ambiguous source, not a certainty -- flagged for human review rather than silently resolved. Science (4, with 1 unit each biology/chemistry specifically required) is NOT ambiguous -- table and footnote agree on the total.
researcher_notes: Found while cross-checking every footnote against its table cell per this batch's audit discipline (see scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md's argument for auditing the whole corpus, not only rows that already look anomalous). The same pattern recurs at REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0018 (Pharmacy) -- in both cases the table's numeric column appears to actually be displaying each school's RECOMMENDED figure rather than a labeled REQUIRED floor, while the prose footnote is the only place the lower, explicitly-labeled 'required' number appears. This pattern does not occur for Business/Ross, Engineering, or Kinesiology, where table and footnote agree.

requirement_text: High School Course Expectations table cell (units of full-year courses): English 4, World Language 2, Mathematics 4, Science 4, Social Studies 3, Other electives 5. Footnote on the SAME page states DIFFERENT, lower math and science figures: 'Students entering the College of Pharmacy are required to have completed three units of mathematics, and three units of science, with one unit each of biology and chemistry. Four units of both mathematics and science are recommended.'

As with Nursing (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0017), this researcher's best reading is that the REQUIRED floor is 3/3 per the footnote's explicit language and 4/4 is recommended/table-displayed, but this is flagged for human review rather than silently resolved.
researcher_notes: See REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0017's researcher_notes for the identical pattern found in Nursing's row on the same source table -- recorded as a systematic, page-wide caveat rather than two unrelated coincidences.

requirement_text: This essay, which can be used for every Common App college or university you apply to, demonstrates your ability to write clearly and concisely on a selected topic and helps you distinguish yourself in your own voice. ... Choose the Common App essay prompt option that best helps you answer that question and write an essay of 250-650 words, using the prompt to inspire and structure your response. Remember: 650 words is your limit, not your goal. ... (The application won't accept a response shorter than 250 words.)
researcher_notes: The Common Application's own personal-essay prompt set is shared across all Common App member colleges, not U-M-specific; recorded here because U-M's own admissions page states the applicable word-count bounds (250-650) which are the operative requirement for a U-M application specifically.

requirement_text: The Common Application includes opportunities for you to share unique challenges you may have faced that impacted your high school experience and/or academic performance. The optional challenges and circumstances question (response limited to 250 words) is detailed on the Common App website.
limitations: Explicitly optional -- do not evaluate a student who skips this as failing a requirement.

requirement_text: At the University of Michigan, we are focused on developing leaders and citizens who will challenge the present and enrich the future. In your essay, share with us how you are prepared to contribute to these goals. This could include the people, places, experiences, or aspirations that have shaped your journey and future plans. (Required for all applicants; 100 word minimum; 300 word maximum.)
limitations: Prompt wording is cycle-variable in general (U-M has historically republished a dated 'Our YYYY-YY Application Essay Questions' post most years per this batch's cross-check with the MIT precedent for the same kind of essay-cycle-variability caveat), but the live essay-questions page itself does not name an explicit cycle/year, so cycle_year is left null rather than inferred from the retrieval date.
researcher_notes: U-M labels this 'University of Michigan Questions' (plural, two questions) rather than a single supplemental essay; recorded as two separate records (this one and REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0022) since each has its own distinct word-count bounds.

requirement_text: Describe the unique qualities that attract you to the specific undergraduate college or school (including preferred admission and dual degree programs) to which you are applying at the University of Michigan. How would that curriculum support your interests? (Required for all applicants; 100 word minimum; 550 word maximum.)
limitations: Same cycle-variability caveat as REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0021.
researcher_notes: U-M's own guidance for this prompt explicitly says NOT to describe U-M generally or restate rankings/statistics, but to explain fit with the specific school/program applied to -- directly relevant if ORYN's advisor ever helps a student draft or evaluate this essay.

requirement_text: Your essays should tell your story, in your words. AI tools can be helpful when used thoughtfully, such as for brainstorming, outlining, proofreading, or organizing information. We recognize these tools may be especially useful for applicants who have limited access to application guidance. However, your application should reflect your own ideas, experiences, and authentic voice. Do not copy and paste AI-generated text or submit work that does not represent you.
researcher_notes: Notably more permissive of thoughtful AI use (brainstorming/outlining/proofreading) than the Penny W. Stamps School of Art & Design's flat prohibition on AI-generated content in portfolios (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0041) or Taubman's cautious-but-not-prohibitive stance (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0038) -- a genuine cross-program difference in AI policy within the same university, worth surfacing rather than flattening into one university-wide rule.

requirement_text: One Teacher Evaluation (core academic teacher or other non-relative who can speak directly to the student's academic aptitude, potential, and classroom performance).

School Report (Common App). The School Report or Counselor Recommendation must be submitted with an official high school transcript and received in our office by the deadline. For this reason, we strongly encourage counselors to submit the report and transcript electronically.
researcher_notes: Classified as supplemental_requirement rather than 'recommendation' because the School Report is a counselor-submitted administrative packet (bundled with the official transcript) rather than an individual evaluative letter, mirroring the MIT batch's precedent for its own Secondary School Report record. Note a phrasing nuance across U-M's own pages: this general checklist footnote presents 'School Report OR Counselor Recommendation' as if interchangeable, while the international-applicants page and the Ross-specific page both instead list 'School Report' (required) and 'Counselor Recommendation' (explicitly 'encouraged, but not required') as two separate, non-interchangeable checklist items -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0026. Recorded as-is rather than silently reconciled.

requirement_text: Submit a Counselor Recommendation (encouraged, but not required).
limitations: Explicitly optional -- do not evaluate an applicant without one as failing a requirement.
researcher_notes: Independently corroborated in identical 'encouraged, but not required' language on the Ross-specific application page (michiganross.umich.edu). See REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0025 for the general-checklist page's slightly different framing of School Report vs. Counselor Recommendation.

requirement_text: Submit your high school transcript. An official English translation is required to accompany the transcript if the transcript is not issued in English by the school. Students who have already completed high school, including university transfer applicants, should be sure to have final high school transcript submitted showing the graduation date. Also provide a detailed explanation of any educational gaps.
limitations: The general (non-international-specific) requirements-deadlines page states the base transcript requirement more tersely as 'High school transcript (additional requirements by country)' without detailing what those additional requirements are; this record captures the detail found on the international-applicants-specific page instead.
researcher_notes: The translation clause is independently corroborated in near-identical wording on the Ross-specific application page ('an official English translation is required to accompany the transcript if the transcript is not issued in English by the school'), so treated as a stable, cross-program university policy rather than a one-page anomaly.

requirement_text: We will allow self reported test scores; the scores do not need to come from the testing agency. ... All admitted and enrolled students who chose to self-report SAT or ACT test scores are required to submit official scores in order to validate their self-report submission. Please arrange to have your SAT or ACT scores submitted directly from the testing agency to the University of Michigan Office of Undergraduate Admissions. ... A significant discrepancy between your self-reported test scores and your official scores could result in revocation of your admission.
limitations: Only relevant to applicants who choose to submit a test score at all, per the test-optional policy at REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0001 -- this is a data-integrity/process rule, not a standalone eligibility bar.
researcher_notes: U-M superscores across test dates ('We will use your highest superscore ... the best sub-scores reported across multiple test dates') per the Application Changes FAQ -- consistent across sittings, no named-exclusion-of-superscore trap found here (unlike the Koç University case documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md).

requirement_text: The admissions process is designed to consider all aspects of an applicant's record and experience and is not intended to admit applicants solely on the basis of grade point averages, test scores, or any other single criterion. ... The U-M application reviewers rate each applicant with respect to the following criteria: Secondary School Academic Performance; Educational Environment; Counselor and Teacher Recommendation; Essays; Awards/honors, involvement, leadership, and service. Reviewers will then balance the different ratings ... They then provide an overall rating ... based on the following scale: Outstanding; Excellent; Good; Average/Fair; Below Average/Poor.
limitations: This describes the university's own evaluation METHOD, not a checkable pass/fail eligibility fact -- it is not suitable for conversion into a structured_rule threshold; included because it directly documents U-M's official rating criteria and scale, useful for advisor explainability (Phase 62) about what U-M itself says it weighs.
researcher_notes: Full rating-scale definitions were fetched but abbreviated here to the five labels plus the criteria list to keep this record's requirement_text focused; the source page's own prose defines each rating band (e.g., 'Outstanding: All of the applicant's materials exemplify superior and/or exceptional characteristics...') if a future pass needs the complete definitions.

requirement_text: Legacy status is not considered as part of U-M's undergraduate admissions holistic review process.
researcher_notes: A negative/absence fact (what does NOT factor into admission) -- explicit and unhedged on the source page, recorded because it is directly useful for an advisor answering a common student/parent question.

requirement_text: Will financial need be considered as part of the application review process in ED? No, we will continue to be need-blind in our evaluation process.
limitations: This statement is worded as an answer within the Early Decision FAQ accordion specifically (question: 'Will financial need be considered as part of the application review process in ED?'), not as a freestanding university-wide statement -- it does not itself explicitly say whether it also covers EA/RD review or carve out any applicant population. Confidence set to medium (rather than high) because of this scoping ambiguity, not because the quoted text itself is in doubt (it was directly read from the live page's DOM via accessibility-tree extraction, not a search snippet).
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT -- searched specifically for an official statement distinguishing need-blind vs. need-aware ADMISSION DECISIONS (not aid eligibility) for international applicants specifically, per this batch's instruction to check for a three-tier in-state/out-of-state/international distinction. Several non-official aggregator/blog sources claim U-M is 'need-blind for in-state only, need-aware for out-of-state and international admission decisions' -- this claim was NOT recorded because it could not be verified on any official .edu page despite a direct search for it (evidence rule: no aggregators). What official pages DO state, and what IS recorded in this batch, is a DIFFERENT and more specific fact: U-M's financial-aid office (see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0032) commits to MEETING FULL DEMONSTRATED NEED only for Michigan-resident undergraduates -- a financial-aid-generosity commitment, not an admission-decision policy, and these two concepts should not be conflated. No official page was found that explicitly narrows THIS need-blind ADMISSION-EVALUATION statement to residents only or excludes international applicants from it; recorded as found, with the scoping ambiguity flagged rather than resolved by inference in either direction.

requirement_text: The university meets the full financial need of all Michigan resident undergraduates who apply by priority aid application deadlines and accept all aid offered.
limitations: This is a financial-aid GENEROSITY commitment (does the university fund 100% of demonstrated need), which is a different concept from need-blind ADMISSION (does financial need affect the admit/deny decision) -- see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0031. Explicitly scoped to Michigan RESIDENT undergraduates only; the source does not extend an equivalent full-need guarantee to nonresident domestic or international undergraduates.
researcher_notes: Same page states 'About 70% of Michigan resident undergraduates and 40% of nonresident undergraduates on the U-M Ann Arbor campus receive financial aid' -- a descriptive statistic corroborating that nonresidents DO receive aid at meaningful (if lower) rates even without a full-need guarantee; not recorded as its own requirement row since it is a population statistic rather than an eligibility rule. Cross-reference REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0034 (nonresident domestic) and REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0033 (international) for the other two tiers of this three-tier distinction.

requirement_text: International students on temporary visas are not eligible for financial aid, and are expected to pay the full cost of attendance. ... There is no federal financial aid and limited scholarship funding available to international students attending U-M, though a short-term university loan may be available in the case of emergencies. ... U-M schools and colleges have very limited funding for undergraduate international students.
researcher_notes: Independently corroborated verbatim ('International students on temporary visas are not eligible for financial aid, and are expected to pay the full cost of attendance') on the international-applicants landing page, the international-applicants requirements-deadlines page, and the College of Engineering's international-students page -- consistent across at least four separately-fetched official pages, no conflict found. This is the sharpest of the three financial-aid tiers: unlike nonresident domestic students (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0034), international students are not eligible for need-based institutional aid at all, only limited merit/emergency funding.

requirement_text: Non-resident students have higher tuition charges because the University of Michigan is a publicly supported state institution and a portion of the cost to Michigan residents is subsidized by the state. Demonstrated, institutional financial aid is available for students and families. Scholarships from U-M schools and colleges or private sources may be able to cover costs for other students by using these combined resources.
limitations: Unlike REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0032 (Michigan residents), no full-need-met guarantee is stated for nonresident domestic students on this page -- institutional aid is described as 'available,' not as meeting 100% of demonstrated need.
researcher_notes: This is the middle tier of the three-tier in-state/out-of-state/international distinction this batch was asked to check for: nonresident DOMESTIC students are eligible for institutional need-based aid (unlike international students, REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0033) but are not guaranteed their full demonstrated need will be met (unlike Michigan residents, REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0032).

requirement_text: All international students at the University of Michigan need both a passport from their home governments and a temporary visa from the United States. ... In order to receive your visa, enrolling students must first fill out the Financial Resources Statement. ... F-1: ... you must offer evidence that you will be enrolled full-time during the academic year. You can do so once you are admitted and confirm your intent to enroll. After we receive proof of full financial support, U-M will send you a Form I-20 ... J-1: If you are an international student who is sponsored by your government or another public source, you will qualify for the J-1 exchange visitor (student category) visa. ... the university or various sponsoring organizations will send you the DS-2019 form necessary to obtain this visa.
limitations: This is a post-admission, pre-enrollment visa process, not an admission eligibility requirement per se -- included because it directly gates an admitted international student's ability to actually enroll, and because federal regulations require proof of financial resources (which links to the aid-ineligibility fact at REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0033: international students must show they can privately fund attendance since need-based aid is not available to them).
researcher_notes: Canadian citizens are a named exception to the visa requirement itself (do not need a visa, but must still pay the SEVIS fee in advance and present the I-20/DS-2019 plus proof of funding at the port of entry) -- a named carve-out worth preserving rather than flattening into 'all international students need a visa.'

requirement_text: Early Decision (ED) is a binding plan. ... The applicant, a parent or guardian, and the high school counselor must sign the Early Decision Agreement, indicating the student's commitment to attend U-M if offered admission. If the student is admitted to U-M through Early Decision, they must immediately withdraw applications to all other colleges and universities. Students who participate in Early Decision could receive these possible outcomes: admit, deny, or postpone. Students postponed will no longer have a binding commitment if admitted.
researcher_notes: MANDATORY BINDING/EXCLUSIVITY COMPANION RECORD, per this batch's brief. VERIFIED DIRECTLY (not assumed): U-M's Early Decision plan IS genuinely binding -- confirmed on the central admissions site, independently restated in near-identical language on the Ross-specific and Taubman-specific application pages. U-M's Early Action plan, by contrast, was confirmed non-binding AND non-restrictive/non-exclusive ('admitted students can consider all of their options, including decisions from other colleges/universities' -- see the researcher_notes on the Early Action deadline record in the companion deadlines file); per this batch's instruction, no separate companion record was created for EA since it carries no binding or exclusivity constraint. THIS IS A BINDING CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENT ON THE STUDENT, NOT A CHECKABLE ELIGIBILITY FACT -- should NOT be auto-converted into a structured_rule pass/fail threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly. U-M is also notable within this batch's research population for having ADDED a binding Early Decision plan only recently (first offered for the fall-2026-entry cycle per U-M's own record.umich.edu reporting, continuing into this fall-2027-entry cycle) -- U-M was previously Early-Action-only, so a stale prior-cycle answer describing U-M as having no binding round would now be wrong; verify current status rather than assuming continuity cycle-to-cycle for this specific university.

requirement_text: There are two components of the Ross Admissions Portfolio: 1. Business Case Discussion: Choose a current event or issue in your community and discuss the business implications. Propose a solution that incorporates business principles or practices. The review panel will look for creativity, drawing connections, and originality. Please limit this response to approximately 500 words. 2. Artifact & Description: Upload a document or artifact that represents something significant about your life to show your learning in action. Describe how your artifact demonstrates your learning in action. Please limit this response to approximately 250 words. ... Your application will be considered complete only after you have submitted your Ross Admissions Portfolio and completed all requirements of the Common Application.
limitations: Submitted via MichiganRossUndergrad.slideroom.com; the portfolio itself is due at the same time as the Common Application under whichever plan (ED/EA/RD) the student applies through -- see the university-wide ED/EA/RD deadline records in the companion deadlines file rather than a separate portfolio-specific deadline row.
researcher_notes: Additional fee beyond the $75 Common App fee: '$5 fee to submit the Ross Admissions Portfolio' (for fee-waiver applicants; full fee not separately stated beyond the $75 baseline on this page). Ross also independently restates the university-wide ED binding-commitment language nearly verbatim (see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0036) and the international-transcript-translation rule (see REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0027) -- not duplicated here.

program_name: Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning
requirement_text: The portfolio is required and is submitted through Slideroom. ... There is a $6 fee to submit your portfolio. ... Document and File Information: One Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) file; 20 MB maximum; Not to exceed 8 1/2 x 11 (portrait or landscape); 8-10 pages, in addition to one cover page. ... Artist/Maker Statement ... 125 words maximum. ... Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) ... Taubman College's architecture program supports critical and responsible engagement with these tools for experimentation and innovation, [but] their use requires careful consideration of issues related to authorship, originality, bias, and academic integrity.
limitations: Portfolio is due at the same time as the Common Application under whichever plan (ED/EA/RD) the student applies through. Applicants to both Stamps and Taubman must submit two SEPARATE portfolios (Taubman's own page: 'Applicants to Stamps and Taubman must submit two separate portfolios').
researcher_notes: Taubman's GenAI stance ('supports critical and responsible engagement ... for experimentation and innovation') is notably more permissive than Stamps's flat prohibition on AI-generated portfolio content (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0041) within the same university -- recorded as found rather than harmonized.

program_name: Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning
requirement_text: Dual degree application/admission is NOT available for Early Decision applicants. ... Dual degree application is only available with one of the following schools/colleges: College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA), College of Engineering, or Stamps School of Art & Design. Students can apply for dual degree consideration for Early Action or Regular Decision, but not through Early Decision.
limitations: This is an eligibility restriction specific to the dual-degree pathway through Taubman, not a restriction on applying to Taubman/Architecture alone via ED (a single-degree ED application to Architecture is possible; only the DUAL-degree option is unavailable under ED).
researcher_notes: A genuine program-combination exclusivity rule, distinct from the university-wide ED binding-commitment rule at REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0036 -- flagged separately because it affects application-PLAN eligibility (which plan a dual-degree-seeking Taubman applicant may use) rather than describing the binding commitment itself.

program_name: Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning
requirement_text: Students will now have the option to apply to the Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning for Early Action admission.
researcher_notes: Listed under 'New for 2026-2027 Application Cycle' (entry fall 2027) -- Early Action admission to Taubman is NEW as of this cycle; a stale prior-cycle answer describing Taubman as ED/RD-only (no EA option) would now be outdated. Independently corroborated by Taubman's own page, which lists Early Action as one of its three plans with its own deadlines/timeline table.

program_name: Penny W. Stamps School of Art & Design
requirement_text: 50% of your Stamps admissions decision is based on your portfolio. ... Your portfolio should include 12 - 15 pieces of your best and most recent work. ... Emphasize experimentation, concept, and a range of media; Include class assignments and self-directed work; Answer the question, 'Why did I create this?' for each work's description. ... Note on work created with artificial intelligence: At this time, work generated using artificial intelligence (AI) cannot be included in your application portfolio.
limitations: Portfolio is due at the same time as the Common Application (page states: 'Early Action deadline: November 1; Early Decision deadline: November 1; Regular deadline: February 1' -- matching the university-wide ED/EA/RD dates).
researcher_notes: $10 SlideRoom transaction fee (waived automatically for Common App fee-waiver recipients). AI-generated portfolio content is explicitly and flatly PROHIBITED here ('cannot be included'), a stricter stance than Taubman's cautious-but-permissive GenAI language (REQ-2026-08-21-MIC0038) -- a genuine, verified cross-program policy difference within the same university, not a copy-paste inconsistency on this researcher's part.

requirement_text: Admission to all undergraduate programs at SMTD requires both a successful academic review and completion of an audition, interview, or portfolio review. All application materials will be considered in the final decision. Our decisions are typically released in the first two weeks of March.
limitations: Exact audition/portfolio/prescreening content requirements vary by specific area of study (individual instrument, voice type, theatre discipline, dance style, etc.) and were not individually enumerated in this pass -- see smtd.umich.edu's own per-program requirement pages for that level of detail if needed.
researcher_notes: Two required components, submitted separately: the Common Application ($75) and an SMTD-specific 'Artistic Profile' ($45 fee; includes headshot, artistic resume, repertoire list for music applicants, recommendation letters, the Common App personal essay, audition date/studio preferences, and prescreening/portfolio/recorded-audition materials), both due by the same Dec. 1 deadline -- see the SMTD deadline record in the companion deadlines file. The central admissions site states SMTD 'programs [are] only available through Regular Decision with a unique Dec. 1 deadline' (i.e., SMTD does not offer separate ED/EA rounds); this record did not independently re-verify that exact framing on SMTD's own site beyond confirming the Dec. 1 date itself, so it is attributed to the central admissions page rather than claimed as independently SMTD-source-confirmed.

program_name: Computer Science (LSA and College of Engineering)
requirement_text: The Computer Science major is open to any student in the College of Engineering or the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA) who meets the declaration requirements for the major. ... Previously, a selection process was implemented to restrict enrollment in the Computer Science major, which required students to apply for selection to the major at the time of their application to the University of Michigan. As teaching capacity has grown and enrollment has stabilized, this requirement has been removed as of Spring 2026. This applies to all students, including: Students who checked the box for advance selection to the CS major at the time they applied ... and were not admitted to the major; Students who did not select the CS advance selection box in their application; and Transfer students who did not select the box for advance selection or indicate CS as their intended major.
limitations: Declaration into the CS major (as opposed to admission to the university itself) still requires meeting separate course-based declaration requirements published in the relevant program guide, which is a post-matriculation academic-progress matter, not an admission requirement -- not further detailed here as out of scope.
researcher_notes: STALE-PAGE TRAP CHECK: a general web search initially surfaced older, third-party-cached descriptions of an 'advance selection' CS admission process still being live -- this was checked directly against TWO separate official pages, both fetched live on 2026-08-21: this page (cse.engin.umich.edu) and admissions.umich.edu's Application Changes page ('The advance selection process for computer science within the College of Engineering and the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts has been removed as teaching capacity has grown and enrollment has stabilized'). Both current, live, official pages agree the process was removed as of Spring 2026 -- NO conflicting live official page was found, so this is recorded as VERIFIED_CURRENT rather than CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE; the stale description that surfaced in general web search results traces to outdated third-party indexing, not to a still-live official page.

requirement_text: Starting this year, Marsal Family School of Education applicants will submit an asynchronous video interview as part of their application for both the Educator Preparation Program (EPP) and Learning, Equity, and Problem Solving for the Public Good (LEAPS).
limitations: Format/content details of the asynchronous video interview itself were not published in further detail on the Application Changes page and were not independently pursued on a separate Marsal Family School of Education admissions page in this pass.
researcher_notes: Listed under 'New for 2026-2027 Application Cycle' (entry fall 2027) -- this is a newly-added requirement for this cycle; a stale prior-cycle answer describing Marsal Education applicants as not needing an interview component would now be outdated.

program_name: Integrated Business and Engineering at Michigan (IBEM)
requirement_text: Applicants to the Integrated Business and Engineering at Michigan (IBEM) program will now have the option to indicate if they would like to be considered for either the Ross Bachelor of Business Administration or the College of Engineering bachelor's program if they are not selected for IBEM.
researcher_notes: New fallback-consideration option for this cycle. Related discontinued pathway noted on the same source page for context (not itself recorded as a requirement, since it describes something no longer offered): 'The Ross preferred admission option through the College of Engineering has been sunset.'

program_name: School of Public Health (Preferred Admission via LSA)
requirement_text: The School of Public Health will be introduced as a preferred admission option for students through the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA). Students admitted through preferred admission begin their studies in LSA, where they can take a broad range of courses and the School of Public Health prerequisite courses. After successfully completing the public health prerequisite requirements, they transition to the School of Public Health for their junior and senior years.
limitations: Specific prerequisite coursework for the preferred-admission pathway itself was not further detailed on this page and was not independently pursued on a separate School of Public Health admissions page in this pass.
researcher_notes: Brand-new admission pathway for the fall 2027 entry cycle -- a prior-cycle answer would not have this option available.

program_name: Bachelor of Arts in Community Action and Social Change (CASC), School of Social Work
requirement_text: The School of Social Work is introducing the Bachelor of Arts in Community Action and Social Change (CASC), which prepares students to tackle today's most pressing social challenges through leadership, advocacy, research, and community engagement. For fall 2027, the two-year, full-time, interdisciplinary curriculum will only be available to undergraduate students already on the Ann Arbor campus through cross-campus transfer. Beginning for fall 2028, it will also be available for external new transfer students.
limitations: Recorded as a NEGATIVE/scope-limiting fact: for the fall 2027 entry cycle this program is NOT selectable by an external first-year applicant at all (existing-U-M-student cross-campus transfer only), and is not open to external transfer applicants until fall 2028. Do not present CASC as an available first-year (or external-transfer) admission pathway for fall 2027.
researcher_notes: Included despite being outside a first-year applicant's reach this cycle because a naive read of 'the School of Social Work is introducing [a new program]' could otherwise be mistaken for a newly-available first-year admission option, which it explicitly is not (yet).
